title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place
abstract: arXiv:2611.21878v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. Such judgments are gradable, carrying both an order and a magnitude. Nearly every benchmark that tests them asks about one entity at a time, then reads that score as the model's knowledge of the domain. Order and magnitude, however, need not be acquired together. Text about social entities carries far more comparison than measurement, so a model may hold a dependable ordering with no anchored scale beneath it. We ask whether a model can place a documented social position on a scale or only order the actors it compares, and what that means for how such knowledge is measured. We test this on party positions in Japan and South Korea, where the Comparative Manifesto Project's coded data supplies a rare external answer key. Asked to order four parties, models beat the strongest fixed-answer baseline by mor

translated_title: 知其序而不知其量：语言模型能对其无法定位的政党立场进行排序
translated_abstract: 语言模型越来越多地被问及现实行为体的立场：某政党的纲领优先考虑什么，某机构承诺了什么。这类判断是可分级的，既包含顺序，也包含量级。然而，几乎所有测试这类能力的基准都一次只询问一个实体，然后将其得分解读为模型对该领域的知识。事实上，顺序与量级并不一定是同时习得的：关于社会实体的文本所包含的比较信息远多于测量信息，因此模型可能掌握可靠的排序能力，但其背后却没有锚定的量表支撑。我们探究模型究竟是能够将已有记录的社会立场放置到某个量表之上，还是只能对其所比较的行为体进行排序，以及这对衡量此类知识的方式意味着什么。我们在日本和韩国的政党立场上进行测试，比较宣言项目的编码数据为此提供了难得的外部标准答案。当被要求对四个政党进行排序时，模型的表现超过了最强的固定答案基线。
tldr: 研究发现，语言模型能够可靠地对日本和韩国政党的立场进行排序，却无法将这些立场准确定位到具体量级上，这揭示了“顺序”与“量级”是两种可分离的知识，也意味着现有的单实体打分基准可能误读了模型的领域知识水平。
en_tdlr: Language models can reliably order party positions they cannot place on an anchored scale, showing that ordering and magnitude knowledge are distinct—and that single-entity benchmarks may misread ranking ability as genuine calibrated domain knowledge.
